claims.text: The proposed WTaTiVZr alloy is equimolar, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has severe lattice distortion.
The proposed WTaTiVZr material has a refined nanocrystalline microstructure.
The proposed WTaTiVZr material can be prepared as a single-phase BCC alloy.
Commercially produced pure tungsten has larger grains than the proposed nanocrystalline WTaTiVZr alloy.
Dislocation motion in pure tungsten is screw dominated and has a narrow mobility mode.
Severe lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr generates wavy dislocation lines.
The high grain-boundary density of nanocrystalline WTaTiVZr enhances dislocation nucleation, motion, and dynamic recovery.
Lattice distortion caused by the multi-principal-element composition modifies dislocation core structures and favors mobile edge dislocations over screw dislocations.
Nanocrystalline grain boundaries enhance dislocation interactions and defect recombination.
Enhanced grain-boundary dislocation interactions and defect recombination delay crack initiation and propagation.
Wavy edge-character dislocation activity and grain-boundary-mediated plasticity replace the screw-dominated deformation regime characteristic of pure tungsten.
The proposed dual deformation mechanism gives WTaTiVZr greater high-temperature plastic strain than pure tungsten.
The proposed dual deformation mechanism gives WTaTiVZr greater high-temperature toughness than pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will show smoother high-temperature stress-strain responses than pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will undergo a delayed transition to intergranular or brittle fracture relative to pure tungsten.
Commercially used pure tungsten typically exhibits limited plastic strain and brittle fracture under equivalent high-temperature loading.
The proposed mechanism is dominant at 700–900 °C under controlled-atmosphere loading relevant to plasma-facing-component service.
Changes in temperature, loading rate, or oxidation conditions may alter the proposed deformation behavior.
Irradiation and processing-induced variations could influence the observed mechanical performance.
